name: mapDeepGet
summary: Reads a value out of a nested map by following a chain of keys, and raises when a key is not there.

arguments.name: $map
accepts: a map, or an empty one

arguments.name: $keys
accepts: one key per level of nesting
a key that is not there raises, and names the path and the keys that are

arguments.name: $default
accepts: the value to answer when a key is not there, instead of raising
null, to ask for the pre-4.0.0 answer explicitly

examples: $theme: (card: (padding: 16px, radius: 8px)); .a { padding: mapDeepGet($theme, card, padding); border-radius: mapDeepGet($theme, card, radius); }
caveats: A key that is not there raised nothing until 4.0.0: it answered `null`, so `padding: mapDeepGet($t, card, padnig)` wrote no declaration and said nothing. A deep read is where a typo is most likely, since there are several keys to get right, and it was the one place the mistake was invisible. It raises now and names the path, the key and the keys that are there; `$default` is the explicit way to ask for the old answer, `$default: null` included.

The other three ways to get it wrong all stopped the build with Sass's own message from inside `map.get`, naming neither the function nor the key: a key missing part of the way down gave `$map: null is not a map`, one key too many gave `$map: 16px is not a map`, and a `$map` that is not a map gave `$map: red is not a map`.
No map the library ships is nested any more: the phone and tablet maps held one entry per device until 4.0.0 and now hold the screen as two lengths. The function is for a map of your own.
